arxiv-2012-02197.title: Addressing machine learning concept drift reveals declining vaccine sentiment during the COVID-19 pandemic
arxiv-2012-02197.creator: Martin Müller, Marcel Salathé
arxiv-2012-02197.description: Abstract Social media analysis has become a common approach to assess public opinion on various topics, including those about health, in near real-time. The growing volume of social media posts has led to an increased usage of modern machine learning methods in natural language processing.

arxiv-2107-02631.title: Reactivity of Ru oxides with air radiolysis products investigated by theoretical calculations
arxiv-2107-02631.creator: Faoulat Miradji, Sidi M. O. Souvi, Laurent Cantrel, Florent Louis, Valérie Vallet
arxiv-2107-02631.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Faoulat Miradji, Sidi M. O. Souvi, Laurent Cantrel, Florent Louis, Valérie Vallet. Quantitative predictions of the release of volatile radiocontaminants of ruthenium (Ru) in the environment from either nuclear power plants (NPP) or fuel recycling accidents present significant uncertainties while estimated by severe accidents nuclear analysis codes. Observations of Ru from either experimental or modeling works suggest that the main limitations relate to the poor evaluation of the kinetics of gaseous Ru in the form of RuO 3 \text{RuO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} and RuO 4 \text{RuO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{4}}} .

arxiv-2203-16765.title: Approximation by Simple Poles – Part II: System Level Synthesis Beyond Finite Impulse Response
arxiv-2203-16765.creator: Michael W. Fisher, Gabriela Hug, Florian Dörfler
arxiv-2203-16765.description: Abstract In Part I, a novel Galerkin-type method for finite dimensional approximations of transfer functions in Hardy space was developed based on approximation by simple poles. In Part II, this approximation is applied to system level synthesis, a recent approach based on a clever reparameterization, to develop a new technique for optimal control design.

arxiv-2209-10530.title: Terrace effects in grazing-incidence fast atom diffraction from a LiF(001) surface
arxiv-2209-10530.creator: L. Frisco, M.S. Gravielle
arxiv-2209-10530.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by L. Frisco, M.S. Gravielle. The effect produced by surface defects on grazing-incidence fast atom diffraction (GIFAD) patterns is studied by considering the presence of terraces in a LiF(001) sample. For helium atoms impinging along the ⟨ 110 ⟩ \left\langle 110\right\rangle direction of the LiF surface, we analyze the influence of a monolayer terrace with its edge oriented parallel or perpendicular to the axial channel.

arxiv-2311-14158.title: Experimental anonymous quantum conferencing
arxiv-2311-14158.creator: Jonathan W. Webb, Joseph Ho, Federico Grasselli, Gláucia Murta, Alexander Pickston, Andrés Ulibarrena, Alessandro Fedrizzi
arxiv-2311-14158.description: Abstract Anonymous quantum conference key agreement (AQCKA) allows a group of users within a network to establish a shared cryptographic key without revealing their participation. Although this can be achieved using bi-partite primitives alone, it is costly in the number of network rounds required. By allowing the use of multi-partite entanglement, there is a substantial efficiency improvement.

arxiv-2407-20025.title: Tropical Tevelev Degrees
arxiv-2407-20025.creator: Renzo Cavalieri, Erin Dawson
arxiv-2407-20025.description: Abstract . We define the tropical Tevelev degrees , 𝖳𝖾𝗏 g 𝚝𝚛𝚘𝚙 {\mathsf{Tev}}_{g}^{\mathtt{trop}} , as the degree of a natural finite morphism between certain tropical moduli spaces, in analogy to the algebraic case. We develop an explicit combinatorial construction that computes 𝖳𝖾𝗏 g 𝚝𝚛𝚘𝚙 = 2 g {\mathsf{Tev}}_{g}^{\mathtt{trop}}=2^{g} .

arxiv-2408-14379.title: Synergistic and Efficient Edge-Host Communication for Energy Harvesting Wireless Sensor Networks
arxiv-2408-14379.creator: Cyan Subhra Mishra, Jack Sampson, Mahmut Taylan Kandmeir, Vijaykrishnan Narayanan, Chita R Das {cyan, jms1257, mtk2, vijaykrishnan.narayanan, cxd12}@psu.edu The Pennsylvania State University
arxiv-2408-14379.description: Abstract . There is an increasing demand for intelligent processing on ultra-low-power internet of things (IoT) device. Recent works have shown substantial efficiency boosts by executing inferences directly on the IoT device (node) rather than transmitting data. However, the computation and power demands of Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based inference pose significant challenges in an energy-harvesting wireless sensor network (EH-WSN).

arxiv-2501-01016.title: Transient rod-climbing in an Oldroyd-B fluid
arxiv-2501-01016.creator: Tachin Ruangkriengsin 1, Rodolfo Brandão 2, Katie Wu 3, Jonghyun Hwang 3, Evgeniy Boyko 4, Howard A. Stone 3
arxiv-2501-01016.description: Abstract The Weissenberg effect, or rod-climbing phenomenon, occurs in non-Newtonian fluids where the fluid interface ascends along a rotating rod. Despite its prominence, theoretical insights into this phenomenon remain limited. In earlier work, Joseph & Fosdick ( Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. , vol. 49, 1973, pp.

arxiv-2505-04806.title: Red Teaming the Mind of the Machine: A Systematic Evaluation of Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in LLMs
arxiv-2505-04806.creator: Chetan Pathade
arxiv-2505-04806.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into consumer and enterprise applications. Despite their capabilities, they remain susceptible to adversarial attacks such as prompt injection and jailbreaks that override alignment safeguards. This paper provides a systematic investigation of jailbreak strategies against various state-of-the-art LLMs.

arxiv-2507-21269.title: Numerical PDE solvers outperform neural PDE solvers
arxiv-2507-21269.creator: Patrick Chatain and Michael Rizvi‑Martel and Guillaume Rabusseau and Adam Oberman
arxiv-2507-21269.description: Abstract . We present DeepFDM, a differentiable finite‑difference framework for learning spatially varying coefficients in time‑dependent partial differential equations (PDEs). By embedding a classical forward‑Euler discretization into a convolutional architecture, DeepFDM enforces stability and first‑order convergence via CFL‑compliant coefficient parametrizations. Model weights correspond directly to PDE coefficients, yielding an interpretable inverse‑problem formulation.

arxiv-2507-22761.title: Approximate combinatorial optimization with Rydberg atoms: the barrier of interpretability
arxiv-2507-22761.creator: Christian de Correc, Thomas Ayral, Corentin Bertrand
arxiv-2507-22761.description: Abstract Analog quantum computing with Rydberg atoms is seen as an avenue to solve hard graph optimization problems, because they naturally encode the MIS ( MIS ) problem on UD ( UD ) graphs, a problem that admits rather efficient approximation schemes on classical computers.

pmc-10646169.creator: Nicholas J. Van Lanen, Adrian P. Monroe, Cameron L. Aldridge
pmc-10646169.description: Effective wildlife management requires robust information regarding population status, habitat requirements, and likely responses to changing resource conditions. Single‐species management may inadequately conserve communities and result in undesired effects to non‐target species. Thus, management can benefit from understanding habitat relationships for multiple species. Pinyon pine and juniper (Pinus spp. and Juniperus spp.) are expanding into sagebrush‐dominated (Artemisia spp.

pmc-11433513.title: Monitoring of Cerebral Blood Flow Autoregulation after Cardiac Arrest
pmc-11433513.creator: Rok Petrovčič, Martin Rakusa, Andrej Markota
pmc-11433513.description: Background: Cardiac arrest remains one of the leading causes of death. After successful resuscitation of patients in cardiac arrest, post-cardiac arrest syndrome develops, part of it being an impaired cerebral blood flow autoregulation. Monitoring cerebral blood flow autoregulation after cardiac arrest is important for optimizing patient care and prognosticating patients’ survival, yet remains a challenge.

pmc-11646472.title: The Prediction of Postoperative Delirium Using the Preoperative Assessments of Frailty and Cognitive Impairment in Aged Patients
pmc-11646472.creator: Pengfei Ni, Ziyou Liu, Jia Yang, Yanhu Xie, Sheng Wang
pmc-11646472.description: PurposeFrailty and cognitive impairment are closely associated with postoperative delirium. The purpose of this study was to compare the ability of screening tools assessing preoperative frailty and cognitive impairment to predict Postoperative delirium (POD) and the association with prevalence of postoperative complications, Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission, and the hospital length of stay.

pmc-11732757.title: Homogenization-circulating ultrasound in combination with aqueous enzymatic pretreatment for microwave-assisted extraction of kernel oil and essential oil from the fruit of Litsea cubeba
pmc-11732757.creator: Xinyu Yang, Yang Yang, Ke Zhang, Ru Zhao, Hao Tian, Lei Yang, Xiuhua Zhao
pmc-11732757.description: Highlights•Homogenization-circulating ultrasound and enzymatic pretreatment was used.•Kernel oil and essential oil were obtained simultaneously from Litsea cubeba fruits.•Ultrasound treatment resulted in increased kernel and essential oil yield.•D-limonene, trans-citral, and cis-citral are the main component of essential oil.•C10 and C12 medium-chain fatty acids are the main components of the kernel oil.

pmc-12374334.title: Molecular diagnostic technology: beyond analytical accuracy
pmc-12374334.creator: Xiangquan Li, Juan Liu
pmc-12374334.description: Infectious diseases cause high morbidity and mortality, and early, effective antimicrobial therapy improves outcomes. However, conventional microbiology methods like culture are slow and insensitive. Emerging molecular diagnostics—such as multiplex PCR (mPCR), droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS)—offer rapid, accurate pathogen identification. Challenges persist in result interpretation (e.g., setting positivity thresholds, low positive predictive value) and clinician trust.

pmc-12468150.title: Pediatric Asthma in the Inland Empire: Environmental Burden, Gaps in Preventive Care, and Unmet Needs
pmc-12468150.creator: Catherine Kim, Christine Gharib, Hani Atamna
pmc-12468150.description: Background: Asthma is the most prevalent chronic illness in children worldwide, contributing to significant morbidity, health care utilization, and economic burden. In the United States, approximately five million children are affected by asthma. This review explores the environmental contexts and lifestyle determinants of pediatric asthma, with a focus on the Inland Empire (IE) region of Southern California.

pmc-12592079.title: Meaning and resilience in war-affected populations during crisis
pmc-12592079.creator: Pninit Russo-Netzer, Ricardo Tarrasch, Rotem Saar-Ashkenazy, Jonathan Guez
pmc-12592079.description: IntroductionThe unprecedented events of October 7th, 2023, in Israel have profoundly impacted mental health and psychological functioning. This study aimed to explore how protective psychological factors—specifically meaning in life (MIL) and optimism—contribute to resilience in the context of wartime trauma. The study focused on identifying which protective factors most strongly predict resilience and psychological outcomes during collective trauma.

pmc-12616988.title: Community beliefs, risk factors, and preventive practices of snakebite: a local study with global perspectives
pmc-12616988.creator: F M M T Marikar, H M P Herath, B M H S K Banneheka, R M A S Bandara, A M M C Amarakoon
pmc-12616988.description: IntroductionSnake bites pose a significant public health concern in Sri Lanka, where misconceptions and myths can hinder effective treatment and increase the risk of complications. This study examined community beliefs, risk factors, and preventive practices regarding snakebites in Sri Lanka and compared them with global patterns.

pmc-12651053.title: Reimagining Arterial Hypertension and Dyslipidemia Care: Telemedicine’s Promise and Pitfalls from the Slovak Patient Viewpoint
pmc-12651053.creator: Stefan Toth, Adriana Jarolimkova, Patrik Bucek, Martin Sevcik, Pavol Fulop, Tibor Poruban
pmc-12651053.description: Background and objectives: Numerous studies and meta-analyses have established the efficacy of telemonitoring for blood pressure and other components of metabolic syndrome in improving disease management. Nevertheless, the adoption of telemonitoring technologies is often hindered by personal, technological, and systemic barriers.

pmc-12999791.title: Recommendations on Drug Selection and Dose Adjustment for Patients with Liver Cirrhosis: Results from a Multidisciplinary Expert Panel
pmc-12999791.creator: Katharina Karsten Dafonte, Philipp Lutz, Christian Jansen, Marika Busse, Peter Dietrich, Katrin Farker, Hans-Peter Lipp, Jacob Nattermann, Tilman Sauerbruch, Sven Schmiedl, Dorothea Strobach, Jonel Trebicka, Dario Zocholl, Gunther Hartmann, Ulrich Jaehde, Martin Coenen
pmc-12999791.description: Background and ObjectivesLiver cirrhosis profoundly alters pharmacokinetics and is frequently associated with medication-related problems. Stage-specific dosing guidance remains inconsistent, and prescribing information often lacks clarity. As a result, treatment decisions rely on individual clinical judgement and may differ between professional groups.

pmc-13518836.title: Development of risk assessment models for microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13518836.creator: Yuhan Lin, Zhenrun Zhan, Ke Zheng, Fengying Zhao, Jiebin Lin, Jiayong Wu, Yalong Tu, Sunjie Yan, Ximei Shen
pmc-13518836.description: This study aimed to develop and validate nomogram risk estimation models for assessing the risk of microvascular complications, specifically diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic kidney disease (DKD), in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted involving 6,043 T2DM patients. Clinical and laboratory data were collected.

pmc-13587573.title: Association of body mass index with postoperative pulmonary complications and potential explanatory pathways in paediatric scoliosis correction surgery: a multicentre cohort study
pmc-13587573.creator: Weihai Shi, Shouqiang Zhu, Yan Wang, Yanhua Sun, Zhiying Zheng, Peiyu Liu, Ruocui Zhang, Tianjiao Xia, Lulu Ma, Min Li, Jinhua Bo, Xiaoping Gu
pmc-13587573.description: BackgroundPostoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) contribute substantially to morbidity after paediatric scoliosis correction surgery, but the relationship between preoperative body mass index (BMI) and PPCs remains uncertain. We evaluated this association and explored potential explanatory pathways and the incremental predictive value of BMI.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 1,165 patients from three Chinese tertiary hospitals.
